boilerplate.general_comments_title: General Comments about the Quantitative Reasoning Section
general_comments: The figures accompanying some of the problems are provided to help solve the problems, but are not necessarily drawn to scale.  Therefore, do not rely on the figures alone to deduce line length, angle size, and so forth.
If a line in a figure appears to be straight, you may assume that it is in fact a straight line.
When a geometric term (side, radius, area, volume, etc.) appears in a problem, it refers to a term whose value is greater than 0, unless stated otherwise.
When \(\sqrt{a}\) (a > 0) appears in a problem, it refers to the positive root of a.
"0" is neither a positive nor a negative number.

clusters.intro: Study the graph below, then answer the four questions that follow. The graph describes a training programme lasting 10 weeks. The participants in the programme do fitness trainings on four of the days of the week (Sunday, Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday). There are four types of trainings: balance, strength, flexibility and cardiovascular endurance (see key). Every week the participants have to do all the “regular” trainings in the programme. They may replace a regular training with any “alternative training” of the same type that is held in that same week (it does not matter what the length of the alternative training is). The regular trainings are represented in the graph by means of shapes without fill, and the alternative trainings – by means of shapes with striped fill. From the second week onward, some of the trainings become longer by a number of minutes from week to week. The minutes accumulate and are always added at the end of the training. The number of minutes that are added to a training appears inside the shape representing it. For example, in the first training week the trainees have to do an endurance training on Wednesday from 8:00 until 10:00. In the third training week that same training will end at 10:10. In place of this training the trainees may do an alternative endurance training (for example, the training that is held on Sunday between 16:30 and 17:30).

Study the table below, then answer the five questions that follow.

The table presents data regarding the number of motor vehicles that were in Tel Aviv in the years 2015-2020 according to types of vehicles.

For example: In 2017 there were in Tel Aviv 209,500 motor vehicles altogether, and 50,600 of them were trucks.

methods.text: Option (3) is \(3 \times 900\) and option (2) is \(1000+900+530\)-ish — both come from applying the 10% to the wrong base.

questions.stem: n is an integer that is divisible by \(3^6\) without a remainder. Which of the following numbers is not necessarily a divisor of n?

methods.text: \(n\) divisible by \(3^6\) guarantees six factors of 3 and nothing else. So any divisor built only from 3s is safe; anything needing another prime is not.
\(27 = 3^3\) ✓, \(81 = 3^4\) ✓, \(243 = 3^5\) ✓ — all within the six 3s available. But \(6 = 2 \times 3\) needs a factor of 2, which \(3^6\) never supplies.

questions.stem:
Given:  x ≠ 0

What is necessarily true regarding the value of the expression \(\frac{|x|}{x}\)?
options: It is positive when 0 < x and negative when x < 0
None of the above possibilities is necessarily true

methods.text: \(\dfrac{|x|}x\) divides a distance by the number itself, so it strips the size and leaves the sign: \(+1\) when \(x\) is positive, \(-1\) when negative. It is never equal to \(x\) except at \(\pm1\).
\(x=2\) gives \(1\) and \(x=-2\) gives \(-1\). The first kills (2), the second kills (1), and together they confirm (3).

questions.stem:
The accompanying figure shows two semicircles whose radius is r.
The points C, D and E lie on one straight line.
Straight line k is tangent to the semicircles at points A and B.

What is the size of the dark area?

methods.text: A negative exponent in the denominator becomes positive on top: \(\dfrac{x^{1/2}}{x^{-2}} = x^{1/2+2} = x^{2.5}\).

questions.stem: Given: \(a^2 + b = (a - b)(a + b) + 13\) Which of the following statements regarding a is true?

methods.text: The right side is \(a^2-b^2+13\). The \(a^2\) cancels from both sides, leaving \(b = -b^2+13\), an equation in \(b\) alone. \(a\) is unconstrained, so it can be any number.

The equation reduces to a condition on \(b\) alone, so fix \(b\) at the value satisfying \(b^2+b = 13\) and try several \(a\): \(a=0\), \(a=7\) and \(a=-1.5\) all satisfy it. One \(b\) working for every \(a\) is exactly what option (4) claims.
The whole question is noticing that \(a\) disappears. Once it does, no statement about \(a\) can be forced — which eliminates the first three options at a stroke.

Yaniv opened a box of olives.  He saw that if he divides the olives among his children equally, each child will receive 7 olives.  Afterwards he remembered that one of his children was not at home.  He ate 2 olives and divided all the remaining olives among the children who were at home so that each child received 8 olives.

How many children does Yaniv have (including the child who was not at home)?

In the course of the third training week Alon gave up the training that is held on Sunday at 10:00 in the morning, and in its place he chose an alternative training. Which of the following durations of time cannot be the duration of the training that Alon chose?
In which training week will there be in the programme a balance training that ends exactly when an endurance training begins?

A man is standing on a platform in a railway station.  A train passes along the platform at a fixed speed of 120 kph.
The train passes by the man over the course of half a minute.

What is the length of the train?

methods.text: Passing a stationary man, the distance travelled is exactly the train's own length.
Half a minute is \(\frac1{120}\) hour, and \(120 \times \frac1{120} = 1\) km. Recognising that the length is the distance is the whole question; the arithmetic is one line.

questions.stem: Which of the following expressions is equal to the expression \(\frac{x^2}{50}\)?

methods.text: Take \(x = 10\): the target is \(\frac{100}{50} = 2\). Option (4) is \(10\%\) of 20, which is 2 ✓; the others give \(0.02\), 500 and 50.

A and B represent digits that are different from one another, between 1 and 9.

Given:  \(\begin{array}{r} AAB \\ -\,BAA \\ \hline 99 \end{array}\)

How many numbers different from one another can the combination AAB represent?

methods.text: \(\overline{AAB} - \overline{BAA} = (110A + B) - (100B + 11A) = 99A - 99B = 99(A-B)\). Setting that to 99 gives \(A - B = 1\).
So any digits one apart work: \(A-B=1\) with both between 1 and 9 and different gives \(B = 1..8\) — eight combinations. The middle digit never entered, which is why so many survive.

Two pipes are connected to a certain pool – pipe A which conveys water into the pool, and pipe B which conveys water out of the pool. Given: if the pool is empty and pipe A alone is opened, it will fill up after 4 hours. if the pool is full and pipe B alone is opened, it will empty out after 8 hours. If the pool is empty and both pipes are opened simultaneously, after how much time will it fill up?

methods.text: Net rate. Pipe A fills at \(\frac14\) of the pool an hour; pipe B drains at its own rate, and the net rate governs the fill.
Confirm the net is positive before computing a time — if the drain were faster, the pool would never fill and no answer would exist.

questions.stem:
Given:  \(2x + 4y < -5\)

Which of the following equations is possible?

methods.text: Every option has the shape \(x=-2y+k\). Substituting gives \(2(-2y+k)+4y=2k\) — the \(y\) terms cancel every time, so the given reduces to \(2k<-5\), that is \(k<-2.5\). Only \(k=-3\) qualifies.
Substitute the four options one at a time: they give \(2k\) values of \(-2\), \(4\), \(-6\) and \(8\). Only \(-6\) is below \(-5\).

questions.stem:
Given the equation:  \(2a \cdot b - 10b = 2a - 10\)
\(b \neq 1\)

a = ?

methods.text: Factor both sides: \(2b(a-5) = 2(a-5)\), so \((a-5)(2b-2) = 0\). Since \(b \neq 1\), the second bracket is non-zero, forcing \(a = 5\).
The stated condition \(b \neq 1\) exists to close off the other branch. Without it \(b=1\) would satisfy the equation for every \(a\), and the question would have no single answer.

questions.stem: In a certain farm the wheat is stored in three barns: A, B and C. The capacity of barn A is 2 times greater than that of barn B, and the capacity of barn C equals the capacity of barns A and B together. On a certain day barns A and B were full, while barn C was empty. They transferred \(\frac{1}{2}\) of the quantity of wheat that was in barn A and \(\frac{1}{3}\) of the quantity of wheat that was in barn B into barn C. Which part of barn C was filled?

methods.text: Let barn B hold 1 unit. Then A holds 2 and C holds 3. Transferred: \(\frac12\) of A is 1, and \(\frac13\) of B is \(\frac13\), giving \(\frac43\) into a barn of capacity 3 — that is \(\frac49\) of it.
Only ratios are given, so a convenient value may be chosen for the smallest barn. The answer cannot depend on that choice, which is what makes the substitution legitimate.

questions.stem:
In a kiosk sweets of three types are sold: chewing gums, candies and chocolate bars.
The price of a chewing gum is one shekel.
The price of a candy is 2 shekels.
The price of a chocolate bar is 11 shekels.
Daniel is interested in putting together a “surprise package” whose price is 21 shekels and in which there is at least one sweet of each type.

In how many ways can Daniel put together the surprise package?
The average of 8! and 10! is –

methods.text: Factor \(8!\) out of the sum: \(10!=10\cdot9\cdot8!=90\cdot8!\), so \(8!+10!=8!(1+90)=8!\cdot91\). The average is that over 2.
Options (3) and (4) differ only in the number, so the whole question is what \(10!/8!\) equals. It is \(10\times9=90\), and adding the original \(8!\) gives 91, not 80.

questions.stem: Given: x is a number that is divisible by 6, x ≠ 6. Which of the following statements is necessarily true?

methods.text: \(x\) divisible by 6 means \(x = 6k\), so \(x^2 = 36k^2\). Since 36 is divisible by 4, \(x^2\) always is — and that holds for every \(k\).
One value kills the rest. \(x = 18\): \(x+1 = 19\) is odd; \(x^2 - 9 = 315\) is not divisible by 5; and \(x - 4 = 14\) is not divisible by 4.
